key_insight: Magnetism governs ordering in Fe-rich Fe–Si alloys: D0₃ ordering dominates in the fully ordered ferromagnetic state, while paramagnetism promotes B2 ordering at elevated temperatures.
engineering_relevance: Linking magnetism, composition, and temperature to atomic ordering could guide processing of Fe–Si alloys whose magnetic and mechanical properties depend on atomic arrangement.
method: Calculate magnetically resolved effective cluster interactions using density functional theory.
Analyze how magnetic state, lattice expansion, and Si concentration alter ordering interactions.
Use Monte Carlo simulations to predict temperature-dependent ordering and phase equilibria.
evidence_signal: For bcc Fe–Si alloys up to 20 at% Si, the simulations reproduce experimentally observed phase equilibria and short-range-order characteristics.
watch_item: The reported scope is bcc alloys up to 20 at% Si; predictions beyond this range require validation.
paper_title: First-principles modeling of ordering in Fe-rich Fe-Si alloys
